programme: ELK1, ETV4 and ETV3 are ETS-domain transcription factors that sit as the nuclear terminus of RAS-RAF-MEK-ERK (MAPK) signaling: ELK1 is the classical TCF that is ERK-phosphorylated and drives immediate-early/proliferative genes, ETV4 (PEA3 subfamily) drives a proteolytic invasion programme (its target list — MMP1/2/7/13/14, PLAU, PLAUR, TIMP1, CXCL8, ERBB2, CAV1, SERPINB3, TERT — is the textbook PEA3 invasion signature), and ETV3's targets (DUSP6, KRAS, FGF2, MYC, MYB, NFKB1, RELA, ERF) read as the pathway's own negative-feedback brake rather than an independent programme.
role_in_a: In Alzheimer's, ELK1 acts downstream of stress/kinase signaling to physically interact with presenilin-1 and promote amyloidogenic APP cleavage; inhibiting ELK1 lowers amyloid pathology via SYVN1-mediated degradation and also shapes neural progenitor fate through DUSP16. ETV4 is implicated in the same axis one step upstream of BACE1: loss of Ataxin-1 raises cerebral BACE1 transcription, and the network places ETV4 at that node — i.e., the module converges on transcriptional control of the two rate-limiting amyloidogenic secretases, PS1 and BACE1.
role_in_b: In esophageal cancer, ELK1 is shown driving ESCC proliferation and migration downstream of lncRNA THUMPD3-AS1, consistent with its canonical role as a MAPK-responsive proliferative effector; ETV4's target set is the PEA3-family matrix-remodeling/invasion programme that this family drives in squamous epithelium generally, though no ESCC-specific paper for ETV4 was retrieved here.
shared_axis: Both a stressed post-mitotic neuron and a transformed squamous epithelial cell can activate the same upstream RAS-MAPK cascade; because ELK1 and ETV4 are the shared nuclear effectors of that cascade, the same kinase input is read out as amyloidogenic secretase transcription in brain and as invasion/proteolysis transcription in esophagus, with ETV3 tuning the amplitude of that output in both tissues.
reasoning: ELK1 has direct, mechanistically specific evidence in both diseases (PS1/Aβ interaction and lncRNA-driven ESCC proliferation), which anchors the module and makes it nameable from the factors alone. But ETV4's Alzheimer's placement is only circumstantial (a BACE1-transcription paper that does not name ETV4 in its title) and it has no retrieved esophageal evidence despite a fitting target profile, and ETV3 has no literature placement at all — so the cross-disease link rests on the shared-kinase reasoning rather than on a retrieved joint source.
support: PMID 41260424 (ELK1 binds PS1, peptide inhibitor of the interaction reduces Aβ production); PMID 40307574 (ELK1 inhibition alleviates amyloid pathology via SYVN1-mediated degradation); PMID 39434411 (ELK1-driven DUSP16 suppression affects neural progenitor differentiation); PMID 40639318 (lncRNA THUMPD3-AS1 promotes ESCC proliferation/migration through ELK1); PMID 31442405 (Ataxin-1 loss elevates cerebral BACE1 transcription — network-attributed to ETV4, title does not name it). No PMIDs found for ETV3 in either disease.
how_to_falsify: In a neuronal model, use MAPK pathway inhibition (e.g. U0126/trametinib) or ELK1/ETV4 knockdown and measure BACE1 and PS1 promoter occupancy (ChIP) and Aβ output; in parallel, knock down ELK1/ETV4/ETV3 in an ESCC line and measure MMP1/2/7/13/14, PLAU/PLAUR and proliferation/invasion. If MAPK inhibition or ETS knockdown fails to move BACE1/PS1 output in the neuronal system, or fails to move the invasion gene set in the ESCC line, the shared-effector account is wrong.
caveats: Brain and esophagus have no anatomical or clinical relationship, so any shared axis here is purely a shared-pathway argument, not a tissue-crosstalk one. The 184 comparisons are built from only 3 independent cohort pairs, so the concordance count should be read as consistency within a small number of underlying studies, not as 184 independent replications. NOTCH1, SOX10 and ZEB1 were excluded as tissue-generic, which is why a MAPK story is built on ELK1/ETV4/ETV3 rather than on a more familiar epithelial or neural master regulator — their absence is the exclusion working as intended, not a gap. TP53 and VDR were left out of the carrying set deliberately: both are strongly and separately documented in each disease, but their target profiles (apoptosis/senescence and nuclear-receptor/oxidative-stress genes) do not form the same recognizable complex as the ETS trio, and folding them in would have been story-building rather than naming a module.
